top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Grossman, with the citation confined to the political economy of trade protection) has the cleanest attribution on the slate. The protection-for-sale papers and the joint book come from one long two-person programme, so no one at the same level is arbitrarily excluded. The framework turned lobbying and tariff formation into a tractable equilibrium object, and about three decades of theory, estimation and trade-agreement analysis show it is mature and durable. The main reservation is that the empirical support for the specific predictions is mixed and specification-sensitive, so the citation should credit the framework and research programme, not claim confirmed results. I rank P002 second because Autor, Dorn and Hanson is now a stable set for a trade-shock-only citation, but persistence and shift-share identification are still being revised and the task-framework antecedents are not credited. P003 comes third because, although the firm-heterogeneity work is influential and densely tested, the exporter facts and parallel models of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum cannot be credited within a three-name cap. I rank no award last because every proposal on the slate is a substantive, mature contribution. I rely on the supplied files and general knowledge, not independent verification, including of the claimed overlap with the 2008 and 2025 prizes.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for Helpman, Grossman, Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Melitz. I am the chair and one of the nine explicit P001 supporters. I am an IIES colleague and frequent co-author of Krusell and Boppart, and a co-author of Friberg, all of whom are committee members and none credited on any slate proposal. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
